catalog_quote: [Wikipedia, Tone] As a tone-language, Pech has two to three distinctive pitch-levels: high tone (á, é, í, ó, ú) low tone (à, è, ì, ò, ù), and sometimes, extra low tone. This lower than normal tone is rare, though it occurs particularly with the suffix ''-rih''. Tones distinguish between lexical items and inflectional types [Wikipedia, Stress] Pech has primary and secondary levels of stress, which are not distinctive. They rely on the underlying marked tone and stem syllables. Primary stress tends to occur in the last syllable of the stem. Primary and secondary stress are also related to inflectional suffixes. ... [Chamoreau 2021 fn. 2] In Holt's transcription, the accents indicate types of tone, and the tilde indicates nasalization. ... In my transcription, I use the International Phonetic Alphabet and I do not indicate tone since the production of tones is very irregular and generally …

audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: both quoted passages are verbatim in the held Wikipedia wikitext (lines 189-194) and Chamoreau 2021 fn. 2 (lines 65-69). But the deciding statement is Wikipedia's paraphrase of an unheld 82-pp Lincom sketch (Holt 1999), and the record itself carries the caution that it needs a primary description. The held primary works (Chamoreau 2021, Chamoreau & Cáceres 2024, CEMCA leaflet, SciELO Chibchan-vowels survey) are silent on stress placement; Chamoreau 2024 has no phonology section.
